result.summary: The intersection provides continuous sidewalks but lacks marked crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps, creating barriers for accessibility and visibility. A large, dense tree at the corner significantly obstructs sightlines between pedestrians and motorists, increasing the risk of collisions.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree at the corner blocks the view between pedestrians and drivers approaching the intersection.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Markings
hazards.description: The absence of painted crosswalks fails to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way to drivers.

interventions.title: Install High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint continental-style crosswalks to improve pedestrian visibility and define crossing areas.

interventions.title: Install ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Add sloped curb ramps with detectable warnings to improve accessibility for people with disabilities.

interventions.title: Daylight the Intersection
interventions.description: Prune or remove the large tree at the corner to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with multi-family brick housing and established sidewalks. However, the environment is hazardous for pedestrians due to a complete lack of marked crosswalks, pedestrian signals, or traffic control signage for the primary roadway.

hazards.name: Unmarked crossing
hazards.description: There are no designated or painted crossing areas at the intersection, forcing pedestrians to cross in unprotected space.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground and at the side street intersection

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corners can obscure the view between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street near the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-striped crosswalks at all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the corners to reduce crossing distance and improve sight lines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to improve sight lines and visibility for all road users.

result.summary: The street features a two-lane roadway with sidewalks on both sides but lacks any marked pedestrian crossings or traffic control devices. Parked vehicles along the curb create significant visual obstructions for anyone attempting to cross the street mid-block.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks visible, forcing pedestrians to cross the street without a designated or protected area.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking blocks the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections or crossing points to improve sightlines.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is highly hostile, characterized by a wide multi-lane roadway with no marked crossings or traffic calming measures. While a narrow sidewalk exists on one side, it lacks any physical buffer from high-speed traffic in an industrial setting.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to cross at least four lanes of traffic without any refuge or marked crossing point.

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: Wide, straight travel lanes and a lack of vertical elements or traffic calming encourage high vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lane with no curb extension, parked cars, or greenery to protect pedestrians.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes or narrow existing lanes to reclaim space for pedestrian buffers and reduce vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.
